# Dependency approvals ledger
#
# `uv.lock` and `frontend/package-lock.json` ARE the dependency graph. Every
# hash below is the reviewed state of one of them.
#
# CI fails when the current hash of either file is not in this ledger, or when
# this file is edited in a commit range that carries no `APPROVED:` marker. Both
# conditions are enforced by `.github/scripts/dependency_gate.py`.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The realistic risk to this repository is not a compromised package in the
# tree. It is an AI agent quietly running `uv add` or `npm install <pkg>` in a
# moment of helpfulness. That edit looks like one more line in a long dependency
# list — it does not look like the start of an arbitrary-code-execution
# problem — and from then on `uv sync`, `npm ci`, the linters, the test suite
# and CI all trust it. No gate in this repo would notice.
#
# So this ledger is not a security control. It is an attention control: it makes
# "did a dependency change, and did a human agree?" a question with an answer
# in the repository rather than a question nobody thought to ask.
#
# HOW TO APPROVE A CHANGE
#   1. Update the hash below:
#        sha256sum uv.lock frontend/package-lock.json
#   2. Commit with a message containing `APPROVED: <what and why>`, e.g.
#        APPROVED: add httpx-retry for the M5 polling backoff
#   3. Get a human to read the actual dependency's own diff, not just this file.
#
# Editing this file without the marker fails CI on purpose. `echo <hash> >>`
# would otherwise be enough to approve your own dependency addition, which is
# not an approval.
#
# Format: `<sha256>  <path>` (two spaces). Comments start with `#`.

04eb9a5cfeb060e03ad424aedf37e62c7932a67750b2f19173c65554c38ff194  uv.lock
2098039027d767db5cdc73beb531bbfe19e5cfbd2b1846fa8bad79d364d0bcf9  frontend/package-lock.json
